A1181.amendmentNote: A1181 replaced A1180 effective 1 January 2025. Covers all wastes having as constituents or contaminants lead, copper compounds, cadmium, antimony, beryllium, arsenic, or selenium. Any legacy references to A1180 in existing permits or contracts must be updated to A1181.
misclassifications: Classifying tested-working assemblies as A1181 when B1110 may apply — document functional testing rigorously
Using legacy code A1180 after January 2025 — all permits and movement documents must now reference A1181
Treating mixed shipments containing even one hazardous unit as B1110 — the entire consignment defaults to A1181
documents: PIC consent from destination Competent Authority
Recovery or disposal facility permit (Annex IV operation)
Movement document (accompanies waste at all times)

misclassifications: Classifying damaged or swollen lithium batteries as non-hazardous — A1170 applies to all non-functional lithium batteries
Confusing with B1120 (functional battery packs for reuse) — B1120 requires documented evidence of functionality
Failing to apply UN3480/UN3481 transport rules in parallel with Basel notification
documents: UN3480 or UN3481 dangerous goods declaration
Carrier authorization — must be licensed for Class 9 DG

misclassifications: Treating drained ULAB as non-hazardous — residual lead paste and sulfuric acid mean Y31/Annex II always applies
Confusing Y31 (spent batteries) with Y32 (lead-acid battery scrap) — both require PIC; Y32 applies to scrap/plate material
Attempting to claim B1120 for damaged ULAB — functional testing documentation is mandatory for B1120
documents: PIC consent from destination Competent Authority
Waste characterization report (lead content, acid residue)

misclassifications: Mixing Y31 and Y32 codes without distinguishing whole batteries from scrap plate/paste
Treating scrap lead plates as non-hazardous metal scrap — Basel Annex II applies
Claiming B1110 for mixed lots containing untested or damaged units — every unit must be tested and documented as functional
Using B1110 for CRT-containing equipment — CRTs containing lead glass are excluded from B1110 and classified as A1181
Applying B1110 to refurbished equipment without documented repair records — refurbishment must be completed before export
documents: Bill of lading with B1110 classification
Functionality test records for each unit (or representative sample per lot)
Commercial invoice with unit description and tested status
If PIC is required: consent from destination CA

misclassifications: Applying B1120 to ULAB without documented functional testing — regulators default to Y31/Annex II for all ULAB
Confusing B1120 with B1110 — B1120 is for battery packs specifically, not general electronic assemblies
Failing to verify destination country acceptance of B1120 classification — some jurisdictions require Y31 regardless
documents: Destination CA notification (recommended even if not strictly required)

B3011.amendmentNote: B3011 was added to Annex IX under the 2021 Basel Plastic Waste Amendments. It applies only to plastic waste that is almost free from contamination and consists of a single resin or polymer type. Exports to non-OECD countries still require Prior Informed Consent under the Plastic Waste Amendments.
misclassifications: Applying B3011 to mixed plastic from e-waste — flame-retardant or brominated plastics are excluded from B3011
Assuming B3011 means no notification required — non-OECD exports still need PIC under 2021 Amendments
Failing to test for PFAS, PBB, or PBDE contamination before claiming B3011

A3210.fullName: Plastic waste with POPs/PFAS — Annex VIII (A3210)
misclassifications: Assuming all e-waste plastic is B3011 — e-waste plastic commonly contains brominated flame retardants (PBBs, PBDEs) that trigger A3210
Exporting without testing — PFAS and brominated compound testing is mandatory before classifying e-waste-derived plastic
documents: Full chemical analysis (brominated compounds, PFAS, heavy metals)

misclassifications: Guessing the classification without laboratory analysis — incorrect classification is a Basel violation
Defaulting to non-hazardous without testing — always apply the precautionary principle and test
documents: Classification opinion from a licensed waste consultant
Hold shipment until classification is confirmed
